sources: Position and job: Wikipedia, 'Glossary of cricket terms' (third man: behind the wicket-keeper on the off side, beyond the slip and gully areas) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_cricket_terms and 'Fielding (cricket)' https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fielding_(cricket); SportPlan, 'Cricket Fielding Positions Explained' https://www.sportplan.net/drills/Cricket/guides/cricket-fielding-positions-explained.jsp; cricketwriter.com, 'Third Man' https://www.cricketwriter.com/cricket-fielding-positions-third-man/.
Who stands there: Wikipedia 'Fielding (cricket)' and PitchVision, 'Specialist fielding: fine leg and third man' https://cdn0.pitchvision.com/specialist-fielding-fine-leg-and-third-man.

The four theories are repeated on cricket websites (Cricket Lounge https://thecricketlounge.com/read-the-story-behind-the-third-man-position-in-cricket/ ; Idiom Origins https://idiomorigins.org/origin/third-man ; cricketwriter.com; the History of Cricket blog); none cites a source. We found no document that settles the origin; the video shows each as unproven.

The 1884 text: James Lillywhite's Cricketers' Companion 1884, 'Diagrams of the Field', ACS online library https://archive.acscricket.com/online_library/jlcc/lillywhite_companion_1884/55/ : "It is the fashion now ... to dispense with long-stop, thereby getting a 'third man' as well as 'mid-on'". The earliest mention we found, not necessarily the earliest.

India v Pakistan, ICC World Cup, SuperSport Park, Centurion, 1 March 2003: Cricsheet ball-by-ball (Tendulkar 98 off 75 balls, first six off Shoaib Akhtar in the second over; India 276/4 chasing Pakistan's 273/7, won by six wickets) and Wikipedia, 'India at the Cricket World Cup'. The shot's direction (an upper cut over third man) is as reported by ESPNcricinfo and Sportskeeda. Field plans are illustrative: right-handed batter, bowler at the top.

long.vo: Third man. The fielder who stands far behind the wicket, on the off side, usually down near the boundary. Everyone knows where he is. Hardly anyone knows why he is called that.

scene.title: THE THIRD MAN
scene.sub: a fielder of the off side, far behind the wicket

long.vo: His job is simple. When a thick edge, or a deliberate steer, beats the slips and races away, third man is the one who stops it from becoming four.

scene.title: His job
scene.sub: to stop what gets past the slips

long.vo: And who stands there? Often a fast bowler, resting between his own overs. The ball rarely reaches that corner quickly, so he has time to recover.

scene.title: Who stands there?
scene.sub: often a fast bowler, between his overs
note: the quiet corner of the field

long.vo: So why is it called third? You will hear four explanations. Not one of them comes with a source.

scene.title: Why "third"?
scene.body: Cricket websites repeat four explanations. We looked for a document behind each of them, and did not find one.

long.vo: Theory one: overarm bowling. When bowlers began to deliver overarm, a fielder was added to the slip and the point, and he became the third man.

scene.title: Overarm bowling
scene.body: When overarm bowling arrived, a fielder was added to the slip and the point. He became the third man.

long.vo: Theory two: the gap. A fielder was needed to cover the gap between the slips and the gully, and so he was third.

scene.title: The gap
scene.body: A fielder was needed to cover the gap between the slips and the gully, and so he became the third man.

long.vo: Theory three: a slip pushed back. One site says a slip was moved back to this spot, leaving two slips, and dates the name to the nineteenth century.

scene.title: A slip pushed back
scene.body: A slip was moved back to this spot, leaving two slips. The new fielder was the third man.
scene.margin: Dated to the nineteenth century by one website. Unproven.

long.vo: Theory four: the boundary. In the early days, only two fielders stood on the boundary. When batting grew bolder, a third was sent out behind the keeper.

scene.title: The third on the boundary
scene.body: Early on, only two fielders stood near the boundary. As batting grew bolder, a third was sent out behind the keeper.

long.vo: Here is something solid. James Lillywhite's Cricketers' Companion, printed in eighteen eighty-four, says: it is the fashion now to dispense with the long-stop, thereby getting a third man as well as a mid-on.

scene.title: Lillywhite's Companion, 1884
scene.body: "It is the fashion now ... to dispense with long-stop, thereby getting a 'third man' as well as 'mid-on', but great care should be used in this matter."
scene.margin: So the name was in print by 1884. That is the earliest mention we found.

long.vo: So the name is at least that old. Where it came from before eighteen eighty-four, we could not find in any source.

scene.title: At least 1884
scene.body: The name was already in use in print in 1884. Its origin before that is not documented in anything we could find.
scene.margin: If you know a document, tell us.

long.vo: Now, a moment when third man could only watch. The first of March, two thousand three. World Cup, Centurion. Pakistan have made two seventy-three. In India's second over, सचिन तेंदुलकर hits शोएब अख़्तर for six, an upper cut over third man.

scene.title: A famous six
scene.sub: India v Pakistan, World Cup, Centurion, 1 March 2003
rows: An upper cut over third man
Tendulkar off Shoaib Akhtar, the second over of India's chase

long.vo: सचिन तेंदुलकर made ninety-eight, off seventy-five balls. India chased down the target and won by six wickets.
So the next time the ball flies off the edge and past the slips, look for him. Third man. Standing far behind the wicket, with a name nobody can explain, and a job that is still simple.

scene.title: Third man
scene.sub: far behind the wicket, with a name nobody can explain

long.vo: What other fielding positions have strange names? Tell us in the comments, and follow for more Did You Know.

short.vo: Third man. The fielder far behind the wicket, on the off side. Why is he called that? Nobody has proved it.

scene.title: THE THIRD MAN
scene.sub: far behind the wicket, off side

short.vo: His job: stop the edge that beats the slips and races to the boundary.
You will hear four theories: overarm bowling, the gap beside the gully, a slip pushed back, a third man on the boundary. None cites a source.

scene.title: Four theories
scene.body: Overarm bowling. The gap beside the gully. A slip pushed back. The third fielder on the boundary.

short.vo: What we can prove: Lillywhite's Cricketers' Companion, eighteen eighty-four, already says: getting a third man as well as a mid-on.

scene.title: In print by 1884
scene.body: "...thereby getting a 'third man' as well as 'mid-on'..."  James Lillywhite's Cricketers' Companion, 1884

short.vo: And in two thousand three, सचिन तेंदुलकर upper-cut शोएब अख़्तर over third man for six, on his way to ninety-eight, as India beat Pakistan.

scene.title: A famous six
rows: Tendulkar, upper cut over third man
Off Shoaib Akhtar, the second over of the chase

long.title: Third Man Explained: Position, Purpose and the Name Mystery | Did You Know Ep 1
long.description:
Third man explained: where the fielder stands, what he does, and the mystery of his name. Four popular theories about why it is called third man, none with a source; the 1884 book that already uses the name; and Sachin Tendulkar's upper cut over third man off Shoaib Akhtar at the 2003 World Cup. Sources: Wikipedia, SportPlan, cricketwriter.com, PitchVision, James Lillywhite's Cricketers' Companion (1884, ACS library), Cricsheet ball-by-ball (our own analysis).
